Marathon Petroleum's stock has climbed 7.81% over two weeks and added another 0.3% today, riding a wave of refining tailwinds. Refineries are running at 98% capacity—near maximum utilization—while crude oil sits around $91-96 per barrel and gasoline prices have hit record highs above $4 per gallon for the Labor Day weekend. For a refiner, this is the exact environment that drives earnings: tight refining capacity, strong demand for finished fuels, and elevated prices customers will pay at the pump.

Geopolitical friction is adding fuel to these higher energy prices. Iran tensions, the war in Ukraine shutting down Russian refineries, and Trump's new Venezuela oil deal all point to a tighter global oil supply picture that should keep prices elevated and refining margins healthy into the near term.
